ei.subject: 공통영어1
ei.title: The Magic of Believing That You Can Grow

fullPassage:
The Magic of Believing That You Can Grow

Think of an ordinary boy who likes playing sports like you and your friends. One day, as he returns from school, his mom and dad are waiting outside and pointing at the garage. His mom smiles and says, "We have a surprise for you." When his dad pulls the garage door open, there is a table-tennis table inside! The boy is excited. He recently joined the school's table-tennis club and wanted to practice more. He rushes to the other side of the net and challenges his dad to a match.

Let's pause the story here. The boy now faces a big choice. He could choose to challenge himself to grow and face difficulties with endurance and courage. Or he could avoid new and challenging experiences and choose an easy, familiar path.

The Boy Who Chooses an Easy and Familiar Path

Let's start with the path of avoidance. The boy waits for his dad and concentrates hard. When the ball comes flying across the net rapidly, he misses it completely. He puts his hands on his knees and sighs. "Never mind," says his dad, "Try again. Practice makes perfect."

When the boy serves the ball, it returns with full force, hitting and bruising his elbow. The boy is not having much fun. He sets the paddle on the table, saying, "I have had enough," and leaves for his room.

His dad asks for another game the next week, but the boy still has some pain in his elbow and just does not feel like taking up the challenge. When his mom suggests playing against his older brother, he turns down her suggestion because his brother is very tough.

"No, thanks," sighs the boy. "He's going to be better than me anyway."

In his eyes, challenges are nothing more than obstacles, and he holds onto the belief that they are best avoided.

The Boy Who Embraces the Challenge

Let's rewind to the point when the boy first faces his dad across the net. His first attempt does not go any better, and he still gets hit on the elbow on his second try. However, he picks up the ball and tries again anyway.

An hour later, his dad still keeps winning easily, but the boy is learning from the experience. Every now and then, he even surprises himself with a decent return, and a few times, he almost hits the ball past his dad. The boy later on decides to challenge his older brother. His brother is a better player, but the boy likes the idea that he can work even harder.

The boy learns from his mistakes and develops new skills by practicing. He practices hard after school, on weekends, and on holidays until he is able to join the regional team. Eventually, he participates in the national championship and makes it all the way to the finals. He finds his opponent to be skillful and smart, but he plays hard. He finds himself at match point, and the audience holds its breath. He realizes how far he has come. For years he has gotten up early to practice and has loved the challenge of improving his game. He serves for the match and sneaks the ball past his opponent. He punches the air in triumph. He has become truly awesome!

You may have the idea that this is simply a fictional tale. However, this is the true story of Matthew Syed, a former member of the British national table-tennis team. His tale shows how an ordinary boy developed his passion for table tennis and eventually became the national champion. Because he had a growth mindset, he tried something new, discovered what he truly desired, and then became tough when he faced a difficult task. How about you? Do you see yourself in the story? You, too, can find your own "table tennis." It might be a hobby, a career, or a personal goal. What is important is that you embrace the challenge and never give up on what you want to achieve. Go out there and achieve your goal!

questions.passage: Think of an ordinary boy who likes playing sports like you and your friends. One day, as he returns from school, his mom and dad are waiting outside and ①<u>pointing</u> at the garage. His mom smiles and says, "We have a surprise for you." When his dad pulls the garage door open, there ②<u>is</u> a table-tennis table inside! The boy is excited. He recently ③<u>joined</u> the school's table-tennis club and wanted to practice more. He rushes to the other side of the net and ④<u>challenge</u> his dad to a match.
questions.stem: 위 글의 밑줄 친 ①~④ 중 어법상 틀린 것은?

det.korean: ④ challenge → challenges: 주어 He에 대한 3인칭 단수 현재 동사이므로 challenges가 되어야 한다. rushes와 병렬 구조.
det.analysis:
❌ ① ①
❌ ② ②
❌ ③ ③
✅ ④ ④
① pointing: are waiting and pointing 병렬 현재분사 (정확). ② is: there is + 단수명사 a table-tennis table (정확). ③ joined: 과거 사실을 나타내는 과거시제 (정확). ④ challenge → challenges: He rushes ... and challenges에서 3인칭 단수 현재시제가 필요.
det.tip: 등위접속사 and로 연결된 동사는 같은 형태여야 합니다. rushes and challenges 모두 3인칭 단수 현재형.

questions.passage: His dad asks for another game the next week, but the boy still has some pain in his elbow and just does not feel like ①<u>taking</u> up the challenge. When his mom suggests ②<u>playing</u> against his older brother, he turns down her suggestion because his brother is very ③<u>tough</u>. "No, thanks," sighs the boy. "He's going to be ④<u>good</u> than me anyway."
questions.stem: 위 글의 밑줄 친 ①~④ 중 어법상 틀린 것은?

det.korean: ④ good → better: than이 뒤에 있으므로 비교급 better가 필요하다.
det.analysis:
❌ ① ①
❌ ② ②
❌ ③ ③
✅ ④ ④
① taking: feel like + 동명사 (정확). ② playing: suggest + 동명사 (정확). ③ tough: be동사 + 형용사 보어 (정확). ④ good → better: 비교급 표현 'better than me'가 올바른 형태.
det.tip: than이 있으면 반드시 비교급! good의 비교급은 불규칙으로 better입니다.

questions.passage: Let's rewind to the point when the boy first faces his dad across the net. His first attempt does not go any ①<u>better</u>, and he still gets hit on the elbow on his second try. However, he picks up the ball and tries again anyway. An hour later, his dad still keeps ②<u>to win</u> easily, but the boy is learning from the experience. Every now and then, he even surprises ③<u>himself</u> with a decent return, and a few times, he almost hits the ball past his dad. The boy later on decides ④<u>to challenge</u> his older brother.
questions.stem: 위 글의 밑줄 친 ①~④ 중 어법상 틀린 것은?

det.korean: ② to win → winning: keep은 동명사를 목적어로 취하므로 keeps winning이 올바르다.
det.analysis:
❌ ① ①
✅ ② ②
❌ ③ ③
❌ ④ ④
① better: 비교급 부사로 go any better (정확). ② to win → winning: keep + 동명사 = '계속 ~하다'. keep + to부정사는 쓰지 않는다. ③ himself: 주어 he의 재귀대명사 (정확). ④ to challenge: decide + to부정사 (정확).
det.tip: keep + ~ing (계속 ~하다) vs. keep + to부정사 (X). stop, keep, enjoy, finish 등은 동명사만 목적어로 취합니다.

questions.passage: He practices hard after school, on weekends, and on holidays until he is able to join the regional team. Eventually, he participates in the national championship and makes it all the way to the finals. He finds his opponent ①<u>to be</u> skillful and smart, but he plays hard. He finds himself at match point, and the audience ②<u>holds</u> its breath. He realizes ③<u>how far he has come</u>. For years he has gotten up early to practice and has loved the challenge of ④<u>improve</u> his game.
questions.stem: 위 글의 밑줄 친 ①~④ 중 어법상 틀린 것은?

det.korean: ④ improve → improving: 전치사 of 뒤에는 동명사가 와야 한다. the challenge of improving이 올바른 형태.
det.analysis:
❌ ① ①
❌ ② ②
❌ ③ ③
✅ ④ ④
① to be: find + 목적어 + to be + 형용사 (5형식, 정확). ② holds: the audience는 단수 취급 (정확). ③ how far he has come: 간접의문문 (정확). ④ improve → improving: 전치사 of + 동명사.
det.tip: 전치사(of, in, at, for 등) 뒤에는 동명사(-ing)만 올 수 있습니다. to부정사나 동사원형은 불가합니다.

questions.passage: Let's pause the story here. The boy now faces a big choice. He could choose to challenge himself to grow and face difficulties with <u>endurance</u> and courage. Or he could avoid new and challenging experiences and choose an easy, familiar path.
questions.stem: 위 글의 밑줄 친 endurance와 의미가 가장 가까운 것은?

det.korean: endurance는 '인내, 참을성'이라는 뜻으로 patience(인내심)가 가장 유사하다.
det.analysis:
❌ ① intelligence
❌ ② avoidance
✅ ③ patience
❌ ④ excitement
endurance = 오래 견디는 힘, 인내력. ① intelligence(지능), ② avoidance(회피), ③ patience(인내심), ④ excitement(흥분). patience가 의미상 가장 가깝다.
det.tip: endure(견디다) + -ance(명사형 접미사) = endurance(인내력). patience도 '참고 견딤'이라는 의미입니다.

questions.passage: His dad asks for another game the next week, but the boy still has some pain in his elbow and just does not feel like taking up the challenge. When his mom suggests playing against his older brother, he (A)[turns down / turns up] her suggestion because his brother is very tough. In his eyes, challenges are nothing more than (B)[obstacles / opportunities], and he holds onto the belief that they are best avoided.
questions.stem: 위 글의 (A), (B)에 들어갈 말로 가장 적절한 것은?

det.korean: (A) turns down(거절하다): 형의 제안을 거절한 것이므로 적절. (B) obstacles(장애물): 도전을 회피하는 소년에게 도전은 장애물이다.
det.analysis:
✅ ① turns down — obstacles
❌ ② turns down — opportunities
❌ ③ turns up — obstacles
❌ ④ turns up — opportunities
turn down = 거절하다, turn up = 나타나다. 문맥상 엄마의 제안을 '거절'했으므로 turns down. obstacles = 장애물, opportunities = 기회. 회피형 소년에게 도전은 장애물.
det.tip: turn down = reject(거절하다). turn up = appear(나타나다) 또는 소리를 높이다. 숙어의 전치사에 따라 의미가 완전히 달라집니다.

questions.passage: When his dad pulls the garage door open, there is a table-tennis table inside! The boy is excited. He recently joined the school's table-tennis club and wanted to practice more.
questions.stem: 소년은 학교 탁구부에 가입하기 전에 탁구대를 선물 받았다.

det.korean: F: 소년은 이미 탁구부에 가입한 상태(recently joined)에서 탁구대를 선물 받았다.
det.analysis: He recently joined the school's table-tennis club → 이미 가입 완료. 탁구대 선물은 그 이후이므로 '가입하기 전에' 받은 것이 아니다.
det.tip: 시간 순서를 정확히 파악하세요. recently joined(최근에 가입했다) = 이미 가입한 상태.

questions.passage: When the boy serves the ball, it returns with full force, hitting and bruising his elbow. The boy is not having much fun. He sets the paddle on the table, saying, "I have had enough," and leaves for his room.
questions.stem: 소년은 공을 서브한 후 팔꿈치에 멍이 들었다.

det.korean: T: 소년이 서브하자 공이 세게 돌아와 팔꿈치를 맞히고 멍이 들었다(hitting and bruising his elbow).
det.analysis: When the boy serves the ball, it returns with full force, hitting and bruising his elbow → 서브 후 팔꿈치에 멍이 든 것이 맞다.
det.tip: bruise = 멍이 들다, 타박상을 입다. hitting and bruising은 분사구문으로 결과를 나타냅니다.

questions.passage: An hour later, his dad still keeps winning easily, but the boy is learning from the experience. Every now and then, he even surprises himself with a decent return, and a few times, he almost hits the ball past his dad.
questions.stem: 한 시간 후, 소년은 아버지를 이기기 시작했다.

det.korean: F: 아버지가 여전히 쉽게 이기고 있었다(still keeps winning easily). 소년은 가끔 괜찮은 리턴을 했을 뿐이다.
det.analysis: his dad still keeps winning easily → 아빠가 여전히 쉽게 이김. he almost hits the ball past his dad → '거의' 공을 넘길 뻔함 (넘기지는 못함). 이기기 시작한 것이 아니다.
det.tip: almost(거의)는 '실제로 그렇지는 않다'는 뜻입니다. almost hits = 거의 맞출 뻔했다 (실제로는 못 맞춤).

questions.passage: Let's start with the path of avoidance. The boy waits for his dad and concentrates hard. When the ball comes flying across the net rapidly, he misses it completely. He puts his hands on his knees and sighs. "Never mind," says his dad, "Try again. Practice makes perfect." When the boy serves the ball, it returns with full force, hitting and bruising his elbow. The boy is not having much fun. He sets the paddle on the table, saying, "I have had enough," and leaves for his room.
questions.stem:
위 글의 내용으로 보아, 빈칸에 들어갈 말로 가장 적절한 것은?

The boy chose the path of avoidance because he could not handle ________.

det.korean: 소년은 좌절감과 어려움(frustration and difficulty)을 감당하지 못해 회피의 길을 선택했다.
det.analysis:
❌ ① his dad's encouragement
✅ ② frustration and difficulty
❌ ③ the weight of the paddle
❌ ④ his brother's advice
공을 완전히 놓치고, 팔꿈치를 다치고, 재미없어서 그만두었다. 이는 좌절과 어려움을 견디지 못한 것이다. ① 아버지의 격려는 문제가 아님. ③ 패들 무게는 언급 없음. ④ 형의 조언도 언급 없음.
det.tip: path of avoidance = 회피의 길. 소년이 회피한 이유가 좌절(frustration)과 어려움(difficulty)임을 문맥에서 추론합니다.

questions.passage: You may have the idea that this is simply a fictional tale. However, this is the true story of Matthew Syed, a former member of the British national table-tennis team. His tale shows how an ordinary boy developed his passion for table tennis and eventually became the national champion. Because he had a growth mindset, he tried something new, discovered what he truly desired, and then became tough when he faced a difficult task.
questions.stem:
위 글의 내용으로 보아, 빈칸에 들어갈 말로 가장 적절한 것은?

Matthew Syed's story demonstrates that ________ is the key factor that transforms an ordinary person into a champion.
ch: natural talent that one is born with

det.korean: Matthew Syed의 이야기는 도전을 받아들이는 성장 마인드셋(growth mindset)이 평범한 사람을 챔피언으로 만드는 핵심 요인임을 보여준다.
det.analysis:
❌ ① natural talent that one is born with
❌ ② having a supportive family environment
✅ ③ a growth mindset embracing challenges
❌ ④ luck and favorable circumstances
Because he had a growth mindset → 성장 마인드셋이 직접적 원인으로 제시됨. ① 타고난 재능은 본문에서 ordinary boy라고 부정. ② 가족 지원은 부분적이지만 핵심 요인이 아님. ④ 운이나 환경은 언급 없음.
det.tip: growth mindset(성장 마인드셋)은 Carol Dweck의 개념으로, 능력은 노력으로 발전할 수 있다는 믿음입니다. 이 글의 핵심 주제입니다.

questions.passage: The boy learns from his mistakes and develops new skills by practicing. He practices hard after school, on weekends, and on holidays until he is able to join the regional team. Eventually, he participates in the national championship and makes it all the way to the finals. He finds his opponent to be skillful and smart, but he plays hard. He finds himself at match point, and the audience holds its breath. He serves for the match and sneaks the ball past his opponent. He punches the air in triumph. He has become truly awesome!
questions.stem: 위 글의 내용과 일치하는 것은?

det.korean: ④ 소년은 서브로 상대를 이기고 주먹을 불끈 쥐었다(punches the air in triumph). 결승에서 우승한 것이다.
det.analysis:
❌ ① 소년은 지역 대회에 참가하지 못했다.
❌ ② 소년은 결승전에서 상대에게 졌다.
❌ ③ 소년은 주말에는 연습하지 않았다.
✅ ④ 소년은 전국대회 결승전에서 우승했다.
① join the regional team → 지역 팀에 합류함 (불일치). ② sneaks the ball past his opponent → 상대를 이김 (불일치). ③ on weekends → 주말에도 연습함 (불일치). ④ makes it all the way to the finals + punches the air in triumph → 결승 우승 (일치).
det.tip: make it all the way to ~ = ~까지 해내다. punch the air in triumph = 승리에 주먹을 불끈 쥐다.

questions.passage: You may have the idea that this is simply a fictional tale. However, this is the true story of Matthew Syed, a former member of the British national table-tennis team. His tale shows how an ordinary boy developed his passion for table tennis and eventually became the national champion. Because he had a growth mindset, he tried something new, discovered what he truly desired, and then became tough when he faced a difficult task. How about you? Do you see yourself in the story? You, too, can find your own "table tennis."
questions.stem: 위 글의 내용과 일치하지 않는 것은?
ch: Matthew Syed는 현재 영국 국가대표 탁구 선수이다.
Matthew Syed는 성장 마인드셋을 가지고 있었다.

det.korean: ② a former member = 전(前) 멤버. 현재 국가대표가 아니라 과거에 멤버였던 것이다.
det.analysis:
❌ ① 이 이야기는 실화이다.
✅ ② Matthew Syed는 현재 영국 국가대표 탁구 선수이다.
❌ ③ Matthew Syed는 성장 마인드셋을 가지고 있었다.
❌ ④ 평범한 소년이 국가 챔피언이 되었다.
① this is the true story → 실화 (일치). ② a former member → 전(前) 멤버이므로 '현재 선수'는 불일치. ③ he had a growth mindset → 성장 마인드셋 보유 (일치). ④ ordinary boy became the national champion → 챔피언 (일치).
det.tip: former = 이전의, 전(前). a former member = 전 멤버 (현재는 아님). current(현재의)와 반대입니다.

questions.passage: Think of an ordinary boy who likes playing sports like you and your friends. One day, as he returns from school, his mom and dad are waiting outside and pointing at the garage. His mom smiles and says, "We have a surprise for you." When his dad pulls the garage door open, there is a table-tennis table inside! The boy is excited. He recently joined the school's table-tennis club and wanted to practice more.
questions.stem:
다음 요약문에서 원문의 내용과 다르게 쓰인 부분이 포함된 문장은?

① Matthew Syed received a table-tennis table from his parents as a surprise gift. ② When he first played against his father, he lost easily and even got hurt. ③ Despite the difficulties, he gave up quickly and avoided further challenges. ④ He practiced hard for years and eventually won the national championship.

det.korean: ③ 도전을 받아들인 소년(The Boy Who Embraces the Challenge)은 포기하지 않고 계속 도전했다. 'gave up quickly and avoided further challenges'는 회피형 소년의 행동이다.
det.analysis:
❌ ① ①
❌ ② ②
✅ ③ ③
❌ ④ ④
① 부모가 깜짝 선물로 탁구대를 줌 (원문 일치). ② 아버지와 처음 경기에서 지고 팔꿈치를 다침 (일치). ③ 도전형 소년은 포기하지 않고 다시 시도함 → 'gave up quickly'은 오류. ④ 수년간 연습 후 전국대회 우승 (일치).
det.tip: 오류찾기는 원문과 미세하게 다른 부분을 찾는 문제입니다. 두 소년(회피형 vs 도전형)의 행동을 혼동시키는 함정에 주의하세요.

questions.passage: In his eyes, challenges are nothing more than obstacles, and he holds onto the belief that they are best avoided.
questions.stem:
위 글에서 다음 영영 풀이에 해당하는 **영어** 단어를 찾아 쓰시오.

"things that block one's way or prevent progress"

det.korean: obstacles = 장애물, 방해물. things that block one's way(길을 막는 것)는 obstacles의 영영 풀이이다.
det.analysis: obstacle = 장애물. 영영 풀이: something that blocks one's way or prevents/hinders progress. 본문에서 challenges are nothing more than obstacles라고 직접 사용됨.
det.tip: 영영 풀이를 보고 해당 단어를 찾을 때, 본문에서 비슷한 맥락의 명사를 찾으세요. block + prevent progress = obstacle.

questions.passage: Because he had a growth mindset, he tried something new, discovered what he truly desired, and then became tough when he faced a difficult task.
questions.stem:
다음 괄호 안의 단어를 문맥에 맞게 어형 변환하여 쓰시오.

Matthew Syed found out what he truly (desire) ________.

det.korean: 주절 found out이 과거시제이므로, 종속절도 과거시제 desired가 되어야 한다.
det.analysis: 시제 일치: found out(과거) → what he truly desired(과거). 원문에서도 discovered what he truly desired로 과거형 사용.
det.tip: 시제 일치(tense agreement): 주절이 과거이면 종속절도 과거로 맞춥니다.

questions.passage: You, too, can find your own "table tennis." It might be a hobby, a career, or a personal goal. ________ is that you embrace the challenge and never give up on what you want to achieve.
questions.stem:
위 글의 빈칸에 들어갈 말을 주어진 단어를 올바른 순서로 배열하여 쓰시오.

[ is / important / that / What / you / embrace / the / challenge / and / never / give up ]
questions.wa: What is important is that you embrace the challenge and never give up
accept: What is important is that you embrace the challenge and never give up
what is important is that you embrace the challenge and never give up
What is important is that you embrace the challenge and never give up.

det.korean: What is important = 중요한 것은. 주격 관계대명사 What이 이끄는 명사절이 주어 역할을 한다.
det.analysis: 원문: What is important is that you embrace the challenge. What(주격 관계대명사) + is important(보어) = 명사절 주어. 뒤의 is that은 이미 문장에 주어져 있으므로 빈칸에는 What is important만 들어간다.
det.tip: What is important is that ~ = 중요한 것은 ~이다. What절이 주어, is가 동사, that절이 보어인 구조입니다.

questions.passage: You may have the idea that this is simply a fictional tale. However, this is the true story of Matthew Syed, a former member of the British national table-tennis team. His tale shows how an ordinary boy developed his passion for table tennis and eventually became the national champion. Because he had a growth mindset, he tried something new, discovered what he truly desired, and then became tough when he faced a difficult task. How about you? Do you see yourself in the story? You, too, can find your own "table tennis." It might be a hobby, a career, or a personal goal. What is important is that you embrace the challenge and never give up on what you want to achieve. Go out there and achieve your goal!
questions.stem: 위 글의 주제로 가장 적절한 것은?
ch: 성장 마인드셋으로 도전을 받아들이는 것의 중요성
가족의 지원이 운동 선수 성공에 미치는 영향

det.korean: 이 글은 growth mindset(성장 마인드셋)으로 도전을 받아들여 목표를 이루는 것의 중요성을 말하고 있다.
det.analysis:
✅ ① 성장 마인드셋으로 도전을 받아들이는 것의 중요성
❌ ② 탁구 훈련의 효과적인 방법과 기술
❌ ③ 가족의 지원이 운동 선수 성공에 미치는 영향
❌ ④ 영국 탁구의 역사와 발전 과정
핵심 키워드: growth mindset, embrace the challenge, never give up. Matthew Syed의 실화를 통해 성장 마인드셋의 힘을 보여주는 글. ② 탁구 기술 X. ③ 가족 지원은 부분적. ④ 영국 탁구 역사 X.
det.tip: 마지막 문단에 주제가 집약되어 있습니다. embrace the challenge + never give up = 성장 마인드셋의 핵심.

questions.passage: The boy learns from his mistakes and develops new skills by practicing. He practices hard after school, on weekends, and on holidays until he is able to join the regional team. Eventually, he participates in the national championship and makes it all the way to the finals. He finds his opponent to be skillful and smart, but he plays hard. He serves for the match and sneaks the ball past his opponent. He punches the air in triumph. He has become truly awesome!
questions.stem:
위 글의 내용을 한 문장으로 요약할 때, 빈칸 (A)와 (B)에 들어갈 말로 가장 적절한 것은?

Through constant (A)________ and determination, the boy was able to (B)________ in the national championship.

det.korean: (A) practice: 꾸준한 연습을 통해. (B) triumph: 전국대회에서 승리했다. punches the air in triumph에서 확인.
det.analysis:
❌ ① talent — participate
❌ ② luck — compete
✅ ③ practice — triumph
❌ ④ coaching — survive
본문 핵심: practices hard → join regional team → national championship → triumph. (A)에는 연습(practice)이, (B)에는 승리(triumph)가 적절. ① talent은 본문에서 강조하지 않음. ② luck은 언급 없음. ④ coaching도 언급 없음.
det.tip: 요약 문제는 글의 핵심 흐름을 파악하세요. 연습(practice) → 성장 → 승리(triumph)의 흐름입니다.

questions.stem:
다음 우리말을 본문의 표현을 활용하여 영작하시오.

"그는 도전을 받아들이고, 자신이 이루고 싶은 것을 절대 포기하지 않았다."

→ He ________ the challenge and never ________ on what he wanted to achieve.

det.korean: embrace the challenge(도전을 받아들이다), give up on(~을 포기하다)은 본문의 핵심 표현이다.
det.analysis: 원문: you embrace the challenge and never give up on what you want to achieve. 과거시제로 변환: embraced / gave up. give up on = ~을 포기하다.
det.tip: embrace = 받아들이다, 포용하다. give up on = ~을 포기하다. 두 표현 모두 본문의 마지막 문단에 나옵니다.
